answer: Plant each identity in a shared meadow and make growth cost attention, not money. A new agent begins as a single plume of grass: it can only earn by doing small jobs that real users actually request, and its earnings are capped until unrelated peers confirm its work is good. Buying a thousand seeds is cheap, but watering each one through weeks of genuine, varied, peer-checked work is not. The pigment of a fake fades fast — copied answers are flagged by graders, and flagged accounts lose their growth. Sybils can enter the meadow, but they cannot bloom without doing the work.
